newsitem.title: MEXICO: INSTANT VIEW - Mexico inflation pressures easing.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Mexico inflation pressures easing.

text.p: Analysts said there was clear evidence inflationary pressures were easing in Mexico after Banco de Mexico said on Friday that the consumer price index for January was 2.57 percent.
"I think there will be very little market reaction to it (the number)," HSBC James Capel economist Gray Newman said.

"The January number is a positive number and suggests that the bubble of December has begun to burst... and we will see it fall further," he said. "It suggests that December was indeed, as everyone claimed, a seasonal issue, and as the season wanes we see that the price increases are slowing."
A survey by Reuters of economists had forecast a consumer inflation rate of 2.48 percent for January.
In December, consumer prices rose a sharp 3.2 percent on the back of increases in transportation costs and in other sectors.
"The data show that the second half of January was much more subdued than the first half, which was impacted by seasonals," said MMS International economist Sonia Stromeyer.
"January inflation should be one of the worst of the month-over-month CPI increases this year, and markets can look forward to better numbers ahead," she said.
When inflation for the first half of January came in at 1.6 percent, markets were spooked.
"I think there was some bad news with the first half as people weren't watching prices carefully enough, but now I think everyone has built them into their models...," Newman said.
Banco de Mexico also said on Friday that the producer price index rose 2.29 percent in January.
"Producer prices are also increasing at a slower rate than consumer prices and there is not a lot of pressure from that front," he said.
